cities.d: second-largest city, and capital since 1997. Worth visiting, but you only need a few days to get to the most worthwhile sights. This city is brand new and being built very rapidly.

x.around: Yandex and Uber were ubiquitous and even in tough weather conditions you shouldn't expect to wait more than 5 minutes for a car. As of January 2023, Uber is reportedly no longer present in the city, only Yandex.

hidden.d: Between Khan Shatyr and the KazMunayGas building with good views to both and also to the Bayterek tower.
The national archives are housed in an interesting circular building with an ogival cupola.
A pair of shiny buildings on both sides of the main avenue, making up a beautiful set together with the Bayterek Tower. Some people think they resemble a masonic symbol.
Shabyt is a palace of arts situated to the right of Kazakh Eli monument. It is a dish like building made from glass.
Built in 2022, this is the largest mosque in Central Asia. This majestic building is visible from quite a distance.
It's next to Pyramid (Palace of Peace) and has a small statue of the first president of the Republic of Kazakhstan. It is about 100 metres tall and has a mythical golden bird Samryk on the top.
An outdoor museum giving you an overview of the entire country in a miniature version. This 1.7-hectare exhibit features more than 200 mock-up pieces, creating Kazakh cities and historical memorials.
39-floor skyscraper in Stalinist style, finished in 2006.

x.intro: Astana (formerly known as Aqmola, Tselinograd and Nur-Sultan), in the north of Kazakhstan on the banks of the Esil river (better known by its Russian name Ishim), is the capital and the second largest city of the country. Modern Astana is a planned city, designed by Japanese architect Kisho Kurokawa. It is home to a range of futuristic buildings, including many skyscrapers.

must.d: The two towers house the senate and parliament of Kazakhstan.

The second largest mosque in Astana and the third largest in Central Asia, completed in 2008. The dome area contains symbols from all over the world like the Statue of Liberty, the fragment of the great Chinese wall, the…
The presidential residence, inaugurated in 2004. It looks spectacular during nighttime when lit up.

An example of the futuristic architecture in the newborn city. Nicknamed Chupa Chups by the locals due to its similarity to a giant lollipop, this 97-m-high building offers a great view of the city as well as an art gallery, an…

The imposant headquarters of KazMunayGas, the government company controlling Kazakhstan's oil and gas exploration. It's made up of two buildings joined by an arch which the avenue to the presidential palace passes through.
Completed in 2006 after a design by British architect Norman Foster, and also known as the "pyramid". The pyramid portion of the building is 62 m high and sits on a 15-m-high earth-covered block.

n.de: Pyramide des Friedens und der Eintracht
n.es: Palacio de la Paz y la Reconciliación
n.fr: palais de la paix et de la réconciliation
n.it: Palazzo della Pace e della Riconciliazione

must.d: Completed in 2012, it's the largest mosque in Kazakhstan and the second largest in Central Asia. A vast calm soaring space, can accommodate up to 10,000 worshippers.

The national museum moved to this location in 2014. The museum is huge and very modern with interactive displays in English, Russian and Kazakh. Popular with tour groups but it's big enough to absorb them.

n.en: National Museum of the Republic of Kazakhstan
n.it: Museo Nazionale della Repubblica del Kazakistan

next.d: depending on the train type 13-21 hours south by train

x.safe: Astana doesn't have any major safety issues, for example you can drive late at night without problems. Bus drivers may shortchange you when buying tickets.

cities.d: largest city, and capital until 1998. Definitely a must-see. Beside the Soviet-style city, you may want to go to the Medeu and other places in the nearby mountains.

x.around: The city is laid out on a modern grid-pattern, and "up" usually means south, towards the mountains. However it's a gentle gradient, and in places the gradient east is also upward sloping.

hidden.d: Honors the men and women from Kazakhstan who died in World War II. There's an eternal flame by the war memorial.
Year-round mountain spa with pools and cabin accommodation. Mixed reviews.
Nurgisa Tlendiev (1925-1998) was a composer who lived here in his later years.
Mukhtar Auezov (1897-1961) was a distinguished Soviet-Kazakh playwright and novelist; he lived here for his last ten years. Atmospheric, but you'll need decent Russian to glean much.
A small museum housing mammoths, dinosaurs and similar.
Military history museum with an emphasis on Panfilov's division and Kazakhstan's involvement in the Great Patriotic War (WWII) and the Soviet War in Afghanistan.

must.d: Completed in 1907 and renovated in the 2020s - new saints were painted in, though presumably they were known to the hagiographers. The iconostasis is spectacular.
Grand mosque with marble walls and spacious decorated interior.

Displays of Kazakh history, from prehistoric times through the Mongol periods to the present. Guided tours in English and other languages are available if you call ahead, and the Hall of Anthropology (1000 tenge extra) can only…

n.de: Zentrales Staatliches Museum der Republik Kasachstan
n.es: Museo central de la República de Kazajistán

must.d: Huge collection spanning Oriental, Russian and Kazakh arts, the Stakhanovite scenes from Stalin's era are fascinating. Abilkhan Kasteev (1904-1973) was a prolific and highly decorated artist.

n.fr: musée d'État des arts Abilkhan Kasteyev

must.d: Small museum with fine traditional wooden facade, exhibits have signage in Kazakh, Russian and English.

n.es: Museo estatal de instrumentos musicales nacionales de Kazajistán
n.fr: musée national des instruments de musique du Kazakhstan

must.d: Russian Orthodox church built in 1909. It was used as stables for Soviet cavalry horses but reopened as a church in 1980. Main entrance is west side from Baytursnov, but there's also a little gate from the park just south.
Built 1893-95 after its predecessor was destroyed by an earthquake, the church became the centrepiece of a monastery, but the complex was crushed by the communists. Only in 2007 were both restored.
Small, brightly painted Russian Orthodox Church with a gorgeously ornate interior.

next.d: Ak-Bulak and Tabagan ski resorts, within a day-trip.
is the new showcase capital, with more of a mixture of cultures than Almaty.
the capital of Kyrgyzstan is a 5 hr drive. From there see Lake Issyk-Kul.
is 80 km long and as much as 300 m deep, eroded into fantastical shapes, especially along the 3 km stretch known as "Valley of the Castles".
in China can be reached by bus. It's on the Chinese high-speed railway towards Lanzhou, Xian and Beijing.

x.safe: Beware of traffic, safeguard valuables and take care when drunk, same as anywhere else.

x.intro: Aktobe (Kazakh: Aqtöbe) is a city in Kazakhstan's Central Highlands.

cities.d: oil capital of Kazakhstan, with large onshore Tengiz and offshore Kashagan oilfields nearby

hidden.d: Beautiful mosque. Entrance only with long trousers. Next door is the grand Isatay and Makhambet Square with a noble statue of these guys on horseback.

x.intro: Atyrau is at the northern end of the Caspian sea in Kazakhstan.

cities.d: Kazakh city in the very north of the country, founded in 1720, closed until 1992 for its military significance in tank production, and home to one very impressive mosque, as well as other interesting…

x.around: Within the city, there are many options for getting around. A fairly simple yet complete bus and marshrutka system exists as does a tram system. Taxis can be taken most places in the city for 350 tenge (2012). Outer regions of the city usually run about 400-450 tenge.

hidden.d: An orthodox cathedral built in the 1990s that has 54 icons.
Here you can walk around looking at relics of military prowess.
A house museum where a photographer who showcased Kazakhstan lived.
Art and even some models of prehistoric animals.
Place to learn everything you wanted to know about the Pavlodar region, its Soviet industrial background, natural history, etc.

n.en: Historical and Regional Studies Museum of Pavlodar Province

hidden.d: This is one of Pavlodar's main diversions, an embankment and observation deck overlooking the turbid, languid Irtysh River, and, when it's not a Siberian wonderland outside, a riverine beach for playing and relaxing.

x.intro: Pavlodar is a city in northeastern Kazakhstan. It is the capital of the Pavlodar Province and has a population of 354,000 (2014).

must.d: Most probably Pavlodar's defining landmark, this striking mosque has minarets surrounding a sky blue dome that is supposed to resemble the top of a yurt. It is named in honor of a respected Kazakh poet and historian.

cities.d: Kazakhstan's third-largest city, very crowded with Uzbek people, it is an old market town located near Tashkent and some beautiful mountains; now booming with oil exploration

x.around: You can take "gypsy cabs" for 300-400 tenge anywhere in the city. Bargain if they try to overcharge.

hidden.d: Old mosque from the late 19th century.
Renovated Russian drama theatre offers wide variety of plays.
Great zoo from Soviet times. Wide variety of steppe and desert species, lots of shade.
There is another small Lenin statue for a backup purpose or if you are deep into Lenins. It is standing on the grounds of a former cotton factory. Free to visit.
On the corner of main street Tauke Khana and Momysh-Uly.
It is a private museum located in a basement of an old Soviet building. You enter backyard and every surface is decorated with some kind of carpet ornament.
There is a whole block in old district filled by a local artist with variety of murals. You start walking around the block and discover more and more murals all over the place
There is a huge Soviet mosaic on building of School #9.

x.intro: Shymkent (Kazakh: Шымкент) is a city in the Kazakh Desert, and is the third largest city in Kazakhstan.

next.d: the most famous Muslim site in Kazakhstan, with a beautiful mausoleum and brand new historical museum. Definitely a must-see if you're in the south for a few days.
. Be warned they drive extremely fast. The marshrutka goes to the main Avtobeketi (АвтоБекеті) in Saryagash.

n.en: parking lot for marshrutkas formally called Kolos busstation

next.d: Locals pay 1,200 tenge for the Shymkent to Taraz road (2019). Drivers don't seem to overcharge. 15-man marshrutkas leave from Samal station, 5 km north-west of the city centre.

cities.d: another ancient city, long a border town between the Persian culture to the south and the Turkic nomadic culture to the north, now majority Uzbek and home to several important cultural-historical…

x.around: Public buses operate in Turkestan. Public transport directions are available on Yandex Maps and 2GIS. A useful line is bus 15, which runs from the train station to the mausoleum via Merey bus station. A ticket costs 100 tenge; cash is accepted on board, and card or Kaspi QR payment may be available on buses with a validator or QR sticker (July 2026).

hidden.d: Turkestan rail station was built around 1906 in art-nouveau style and with adjacent blocks is a great example of railway architecture
Semi-underground mosque.

x.intro: Turkestan or Turkistan (Kazakh: Түркістан Türkistan) is a small but ancient city in the Kazakh Desert. There are many historical sights in this relatively well preserved, 1600-year-old city.

must.d: Commissioned in 1389 for the 12th-century Sufi poet and mystic Khoja Ahmed Yasawi, but never finished. This mausoleum is nevertheless a major destinations for pilgrimages from across Central Asia and has come to epitomize the…

next.d: The line mini buses cartels going to Shymkent have a sort of monopoly and it's more expensive from Turkestan than the opposite.

intro: Kazakhstan (Kazakh: Қазақстан Qazaqstan; Russian: Казахстан) is the largest of the states of the former Soviet Union apart from Russia, and it dwarfs the other countries of Central Asia and stretches into Eastern Europe. Kazakhstan is the richest country in the region due to its large oil and natural gas reserves and is also the largest in Central Asia.

x.intro: Baikonur (Kazakh: Байқоңыр Bayqongyr, Russian: Байконур Baykonur) is a city in Kazakhstan but is administered by the Russian government.

must.d: A lot of Russia's space exploration missions were launched from here. Permits are necessary and must be arranged at least 45 days in advance; the only practical way of doing this is through a specialist travel agency.

x.around: If you wish to see the Kent Mountains, you will need to purchase a tour package from the park administration. They will use their transportation to guide you. Advanced notice of a week is needed for this.
x.intro: Karkaraly National Park (Kazakh: Қарқаралы мемлекеттік ұлттық табиғи паркі) (Russian: Каркаралинский государственный национальный природный парк) is a protected reserve and national park in the Karaganda Oblast in the Central Highlands of Kazakhstan. The park headquarters are in the city of Karkaraly, 244 km east of Karaganda.
